course.title: Bread and Pastry Baking
course.tagline: Bake soft bread, meat pies and pastries from scratch, ready to sell.

days.title: Baking Basics: What You Need
days.goal: Know your tools, your ingredients, and how an oven works.

video.title: HOW This 1-Minute Dough Makes Better Bread Than Your Bakery

steps: Find your tools: a big bowl, a baking tray, a rolling pin, and a clean cloth.
Learn the main ingredients: flour, yeast, sugar, salt, butter, and eggs.
Yeast is a tiny living thing that makes dough rise. Keep it dry and cool.
Learn your oven: preheat means turn it on early so it is hot before the food goes in.
Weigh or measure your ingredients. Baking needs exact amounts.
days.task: List your baking tools and ingredients, and test your oven temperature.
days.challenge: Bake nothing today. Just set up your space so it is clean and ready.

quiz.q: What does 'preheat' mean?
options: Turn the oven on early so it is hot before baking
Put food in a cold oven
quiz.explain: Preheating means the oven is at the right heat before the food goes in.

quiz.q: What does yeast do in dough?
quiz.explain: Yeast makes gas in the dough, and the gas makes the dough rise.

quiz.q: Why must baking amounts be exact?
options: Too much or too little of one thing can spoil the bake
quiz.explain: Baking is like a recipe for a cake: wrong amounts give a wrong result.

days.title: Your First White Bread
days.goal: Bake a simple white loaf from scratch.

video.title: The Easiest Sourdough Bread for Beginners! No Kneading, Just 4 Ingredients

steps: Mix flour, yeast, salt, and warm water in a big bowl.
Stir until it forms a soft dough. It will feel sticky at first.
Knead means push and fold the dough for 10 minutes until it feels smooth.
Cover the bowl with a cloth. Leave it for 1 hour until it doubles in size.
Shape it into a loaf. Bake at 200°C for 25 to 30 minutes.
days.task: Bake one white loaf.
days.challenge: Tap the bottom of the loaf. If it sounds hollow, it is done.

quiz.q: What is kneading?
options: Pushing and folding dough until it is smooth
quiz.explain: Kneading pushes and folds the dough so it becomes smooth and stretchy.

quiz.q: How do you know dough has risen enough?
quiz.explain: Risen dough is about twice as big as when you started.

quiz.q: Why tap the bottom of a loaf?
options: A hollow sound means it is baked through
quiz.explain: A hollow tap means the inside is cooked, not doughy.

days.title: No-Knead Bread: The Easy Way
days.goal: Bake bread without kneading, using time instead of effort.

video.title: The Easiest Butter Bread: No Kneading! Tastier than store-bought

steps: Mix flour, a little yeast, salt, and water. Stir only until mixed.
Cover the bowl. Leave it on the counter for 12 to 18 hours.
The dough will bubble and rise slowly on its own.
Shape it gently. Do not punch all the air out.
Bake in a hot oven until the crust is golden and crisp.
days.task: Mix a no-knead dough tonight and bake it tomorrow.
days.challenge: Compare the no-knead loaf with yesterday's loaf. Which crust do you like more?

quiz.q: What does no-knead bread use instead of kneading?
quiz.explain: A long slow rise does the work that kneading does.

quiz.q: Why not punch all the air out when shaping?
options: The air bubbles make the bread light
quiz.explain: Air bubbles in the dough make the bread light and full of holes.

quiz.q: How long does no-knead dough rest?
quiz.explain: No-knead dough rests overnight, 12 to 18 hours.

days.title: Butter Bread: Soft and Rich
days.goal: Bake a soft butter bread that stays fresh for days.

video.title: Puff Pastry and Minced Meat Appetizer with a Trick That Few People Know!

steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt, milk, and soft butter.
Knead for 10 minutes until the dough is smooth and a little shiny.
Let it rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Shape into a loaf or rolls. Brush the top with milk.
Bake at 180°C until golden. Brush with butter while still warm.
days.task: Bake a butter bread loaf.
days.challenge: Make the same dough into 8 small rolls instead of one loaf.

quiz.q: What makes butter bread soft?
options: Butter and milk in the dough
quiz.explain: Butter and milk make the crumb soft and rich.

quiz.q: Why brush the top with milk before baking?
options: It helps the top turn golden
quiz.explain: Milk on top helps the crust brown nicely.

quiz.q: Why brush butter on warm bread?
options: To make it last longer only
quiz.explain: Butter brushed on warm bread melts in and adds flavour and shine.

days.title: Sourdough for Beginners
days.goal: Start a simple sourdough loaf with just four things.

video.title: Minced Meat Puff Pastry So Tasty That Everyone Will Ask for the Recipe!

steps: Sourdough uses a starter: a mix of flour and water that has sat for days.
If you have no starter, use a little yeast and a long rest instead.
Mix flour, water, salt, and your starter or yeast.
Let it rise slowly for several hours. Fold it a few times.
Bake in a very hot oven for a crisp crust.
days.task: Bake a simple sourdough-style loaf.
days.challenge: Start your own starter: mix flour and water in a jar and feed it daily.

quiz.q: What is a sourdough starter?
options: Flour and water left to ferment, full of good yeast
quiz.explain: A starter is flour and water that has fermented and is full of wild yeast.

quiz.q: Why fold the dough instead of kneading it?
options: Folding is gentle and keeps the air in
quiz.explain: Gentle folding builds strength without pushing the air out.

quiz.q: Why bake sourdough in a very hot oven?
options: High heat gives a crisp crust
quiz.explain: A very hot oven makes the crust crisp and the loaf rise fast.

days.title: Measuring and Mixing Like a Baker
days.goal: Measure well and mix dough the right way.

video.title: 10 Minutes Snack! Easy Flaky Meat Pie with Puff Pastry

steps: Use a scale if you have one. It is more exact than cups.
Spoon flour into a cup and level it off. Do not pack it down.
Add water a little at a time. You can always add more.
Mix until there is no dry flour left, then stop.
Write down what you used so you can repeat a good bake.
days.task: Bake a loaf using a scale, and write down every amount.
days.challenge: Bake the same loaf using cups and see if the result is different.

quiz.q: Why is a scale better than cups for baking?
quiz.explain: A scale measures the true weight, so every bake is the same.

quiz.q: Why add water a little at a time?
options: You can add more but you cannot take it out
quiz.explain: Too much water makes sticky dough that is hard to fix.

quiz.q: Why write down your amounts?
options: So you can repeat a good bake
quiz.explain: Notes let you repeat what worked and fix what did not.

days.title: Week 1 Project: Bake Three Breads
days.goal: Bake three different breads and compare them.

video.title: I Stopped Rolling Dough — Now I Bake Dinner Pies This Way

steps: Pick three breads from this week: white, no-knead, and butter bread.
Make a shopping list and buy everything in one trip.
Start the no-knead dough the night before.
Bake one loaf at a time so the oven is free.
Taste all three with your household and pick a favourite.
days.task: Bake three different breads in one day.
days.challenge: Give one loaf to a neighbour and ask what they think.

quiz.q: Why start the no-knead dough the night before?
options: It needs 12 to 18 hours to rise
quiz.explain: No-knead dough rises slowly overnight.

quiz.q: Why bake one loaf at a time?
options: So each loaf gets full oven heat
quiz.explain: One loaf at a time gets even heat and a better rise.

quiz.q: What should you compare between breads?
options: Crust, softness, taste, and how long they stay fresh
quiz.explain: Crust, softness, taste, and freshness tell you which bread is best.

project.title: Bake Three Different Breads
project.brief: Bake a white loaf, a no-knead loaf, and a butter bread in one day.
checks: Three different breads baked
No-knead dough started the night before
Each loaf risen well and baked through
Crusts golden, insides soft and not doughy
All three tasted and compared
Favourite picked and noted down

days.title: Puff Puff: The Nigerian Favourite
days.goal: Make puff puff, the sweet fried dough balls.

video.title: Spanish Puff Pastry Meat Pie (Murcia-Style)

steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt, and warm water into a thick batter.
Cover and leave for 1 hour until it rises and bubbles.
Heat oil in a deep pot. Test with a drop of batter: it should rise at once.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the oil. Turn them until golden all over.
Drain on paper and serve warm.
days.task: Make a batch of puff puff.
days.challenge: Try a second batch with a little nutmeg or vanilla and compare.

quiz.q: How thick should puff puff batter be?
options: Thick, so it holds its shape on a spoon
quiz.explain: Thick batter holds its shape and fries into round balls.

quiz.q: How do you know the oil is hot enough?
options: A drop of batter rises at once
quiz.explain: Batter that rises at once means the oil is ready.

quiz.q: Why turn puff puff while frying?
options: So it browns evenly all over
quiz.explain: Turning gives an even golden colour on all sides.

days.title: Meat Pie: The Classic Snack
days.goal: Make Nigerian meat pie with a flaky crust.

video.title: Nigerian Puff Puff Recipe: How to Make Puff Puff

steps: Make the filling: fry minced meat with onion, carrot, and potato.
Season well and let the filling cool. Hot filling melts the pastry.
Make the pastry: rub butter into flour until it looks like crumbs.
Add cold water a little at a time until it forms a dough.
Roll out, cut circles, fill, fold, seal, and bake until golden.
days.task: Bake a batch of meat pies.
days.challenge: Make a second batch with chicken filling instead of beef.

quiz.q: Why must meat pie filling be cool before filling?
quiz.explain: Hot filling melts the butter in the pastry and makes it soggy.

quiz.q: What does rubbing butter into flour do?
quiz.explain: Butter mixed into flour in crumbs makes a flaky crust.

quiz.q: Why use cold water for pastry?
options: Cold water keeps the butter solid so the pastry stays flaky
quiz.explain: Warm water melts the butter and ruins the flaky layers.

days.title: Puff Pastry: Layers of Butter
days.goal: Use puff pastry to make quick, flaky snacks.

video.title: You'll Never Need Another Puff Puff Recipe Again | Street Snacks Ep. 17

steps: Buy ready-made puff pastry or make a simple version at home.
Keep it cold. Warm pastry sticks and will not puff.
Cut into squares. Add a spoon of minced meat or cheese.
Fold and press the edges with a fork to seal.
Bake at 200°C until puffed up and golden.
days.task: Make puff pastry meat snacks.
days.challenge: Make a sweet version with jam or sugar and compare.

quiz.q: Why must puff pastry stay cold?
options: Warm pastry sticks and will not puff up
quiz.explain: Cold butter in the pastry turns to steam in the oven and lifts the layers.

quiz.q: What makes puff pastry rise?
quiz.explain: Butter between the layers turns to steam and pushes the layers apart.

quiz.q: Why seal the edges with a fork?
options: So the filling does not leak out
quiz.explain: Sealed edges keep the filling inside while it bakes.

days.title: Dinner Pies Without Rolling
days.goal: Make a dinner pie the easy way, with no rolling pin.

video.title: Puff Puff (West African Doughnuts)

steps: Grease a baking dish and line it with pastry or bread dough.
Add your filling: meat, vegetables, and sauce.
Cover the top with more pastry or a lid of dough.
Cut a small hole in the top so steam can escape.
Bake until golden and bubbling. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.
days.task: Bake a dinner pie.
days.challenge: Make a second pie with a different filling and note which one your household likes best.

quiz.q: Why cut a hole in the top of a pie?
options: So steam escapes and the pastry stays crisp
To check if it is done
quiz.explain: Steam trapped inside makes the pastry soggy.

quiz.q: Why rest a pie before cutting?
options: The filling sets so slices hold together
quiz.explain: Resting lets the hot filling firm up so slices do not fall apart.

quiz.q: What can you use instead of a rolling pin?
quiz.explain: You can press dough into a dish with your hands or roll it with a clean bottle.

days.title: Scones and Small Bakes
days.goal: Bake scones and other small, quick bakes.

video.title: Quarantine Cooking: African Doughnuts

steps: Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and cold butter.
Rub the butter in until it looks like crumbs.
Add milk and mix just until it comes together. Do not over-mix.
Cut into rounds and bake at 200°C for 12 to 15 minutes.
Serve warm with butter and jam.
days.task: Bake a batch of scones.
days.challenge: Add raisins or cheese to half the batch and compare.

quiz.q: What makes scones rise?
quiz.explain: Baking powder makes gas when heated, so scones rise fast.

quiz.q: Why not over-mix scone dough?
quiz.explain: Too much mixing makes tough, hard scones.

quiz.q: How long do scones bake?
quiz.explain: Scones are small, so they bake in 12 to 15 minutes.

days.title: Baking for Selling: Cost Your Bakes
days.goal: Work out what your bakes cost and what to charge.

video.title: EXTRA CRISPY Bread in 5 Minutes! No Kneading, Just Mix and Bake

steps: List every ingredient with its price.
Add gas and packaging costs.
Divide the total by the number of pieces you made.
Charge 2 to 3 times the cost per piece for a profit.
Compare with bakery prices near you.
days.task: Cost a batch of puff puff and set a selling price per piece.
days.challenge: Cost a batch of meat pies the same way.

quiz.q: What is the cost per piece?
options: Total cost divided by the number of pieces
quiz.explain: Cost per piece is the total cost shared across all the pieces you made.

quiz.q: Why charge 2 to 3 times the cost?
options: To cover gas, packaging, and your time, and still make a profit
quiz.explain: The extra covers all the costs beyond ingredients and leaves profit.

quiz.q: What else must you add to the cost?
quiz.explain: Gas and packaging are real costs of every bake.

days.title: Week 2 Project: A Snack Box
days.goal: Bake a snack box with puff puff, meat pie, and scones.

video.title: Easiest Homemade White Bread Recipe: No Fancy Tools Needed

steps: Plan the box: puff puff, meat pie, and scones.
Write a shopping list with costs.
Make the meat pie filling first and let it cool.
Bake the meat pies, then the scones, then fry the puff puff.
Pack the box neatly and share it with friends or family.
days.task: Bake a snack box with three items.
days.challenge: Price the whole box as if you were selling it.

quiz.q: Why make the filling first?
options: It needs time to cool before it goes into pastry
quiz.explain: Filling must be cool, or it melts the pastry.

quiz.q: What order should you bake in?
options: Longest first, so all finish together
quiz.explain: Start with what takes longest so everything is ready together.

quiz.q: Why price the box as if selling it?
options: It teaches you the real cost of your work
quiz.explain: Pricing practice turns baking into a business skill.

project.title: Bake a Three-Item Snack Box
project.brief: Bake puff puff, meat pie, and scones, and pack them as one snack box.
checks: Three different snacks baked or fried
Meat pie filling made and cooled first
Pastry golden and flaky, not soggy
Puff puff golden all over
Scones risen and soft inside
Box packed neatly and priced

days.title: Buns and Rolls: Soft and Sweet
days.goal: Bake soft buns and rolls for breakfast and snacks.

video.title: HOW This 1-Minute Dough Makes Better Bread Than Your Bakery

steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, milk, and butter into a soft dough.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth.
Let it rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Shape into small balls. Place them close together in a tray.
Bake at 180°C until golden. Brush with butter.
days.task: Bake a tray of soft buns.
days.challenge: Fill half the buns with jam or chocolate before baking.

quiz.q: Why place buns close together?
options: They rise into each other and stay soft
quiz.explain: Buns baked close together stay soft on the sides.

quiz.q: What makes buns sweet?
quiz.explain: Sugar in the dough makes the buns sweet.

quiz.q: Why brush buns with butter after baking?
options: To make them last longer only
quiz.explain: Butter on warm buns adds shine and a rich taste.

days.title: Flatbread and Chapati
days.goal: Make flatbread on the stove, no oven needed.

video.title: The Easiest Sourdough Bread for Beginners! No Kneading, Just 4 Ingredients

steps: Mix flour, salt, and warm water into a soft dough.
Knead for 5 minutes. Rest for 30 minutes.
Roll each piece into a thin circle.
Cook in a hot dry pan for 1 minute each side until puffed and spotted.
Brush with butter and keep warm under a cloth.
days.task: Make flatbreads on the stove.
days.challenge: Make a second batch with a little garlic butter and compare.

quiz.q: Why rest flatbread dough?
options: Resting makes it soft and easy to roll
quiz.explain: Resting relaxes the dough so it rolls out thin without springing back.

quiz.q: How do you know flatbread is done?
options: It puffs up and gets brown spots
quiz.explain: Puffing and brown spots mean it is cooked through.

quiz.q: Why keep flatbread under a cloth?
options: To keep it warm and soft
quiz.explain: A cloth traps steam and keeps the bread soft.

days.title: Doughnuts: Fried and Glazed
days.goal: Make doughnuts at home and glaze them simply.

video.title: The Easiest Butter Bread: No Kneading! Tastier than store-bought

steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, milk, butter, and egg into a soft dough.
Let it rise for 1 hour. Roll out and cut rings.
Let the rings rise again for 30 minutes.
Fry in hot oil for 1 minute each side until golden.
Dip in a simple glaze of icing sugar and milk.
days.task: Make a batch of doughnuts.
days.challenge: Try a second batch with a chocolate glaze.

quiz.q: Why let doughnut rings rise a second time?
options: A second rise makes them light and fluffy
quiz.explain: The second rise fills the rings with air so they fry up light.

quiz.q: How long do doughnuts fry?
quiz.explain: Doughnuts are small and fry fast, about 1 minute per side.

quiz.q: What is a simple glaze?
options: Icing sugar mixed with a little milk
quiz.explain: Icing sugar and a little milk make a simple sweet glaze.

days.title: Banana Bread: Use Up Ripe Bananas
days.goal: Bake banana bread with bananas that are too ripe to eat.

video.title: Puff Pastry and Minced Meat Appetizer with a Trick That Few People Know!

steps: Mash 3 very ripe bananas in a bowl.
Add sugar, melted butter, eggs, and a little vanilla.
Stir in flour and baking soda. Do not over-mix.
Pour into a lined loaf tin.
Bake at 180°C for 50 to 60 minutes. Test with a toothpick.
days.task: Bake a banana bread loaf.
days.challenge: Add nuts or chocolate chips to the next loaf.

quiz.q: Why use very ripe bananas?
options: Ripe bananas are sweeter and softer
quiz.explain: Very ripe bananas are sweet and mash easily.

quiz.q: How do you test if banana bread is done?
quiz.explain: A clean toothpick means the middle is cooked.

quiz.q: Why not over-mix banana bread?
quiz.explain: Too much mixing makes the bread tough instead of soft.

days.title: Pastry for Beginners: Shortcrust
days.goal: Make shortcrust pastry for tarts and pies.

video.title: Minced Meat Puff Pastry So Tasty That Everyone Will Ask for the Recipe!

steps: Rub cold butter into flour until it looks like fine crumbs.
Add a pinch of salt and a little cold water.
Bring it together into a dough. Do not knead it.
Wrap and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Roll out and line a tin. Fill and bake.
days.task: Make a shortcrust tart with a jam or fruit filling.
days.challenge: Make a savoury tart with egg and cheese filling.

quiz.q: Why chill shortcrust pastry?
options: Chilling keeps the butter cold so the pastry is crisp
quiz.explain: Cold butter in the pastry gives a crisp, crumbly result.

quiz.q: Why not knead shortcrust?
quiz.explain: Kneading builds stretch in the dough and makes pastry tough.

quiz.q: What is shortcrust used for?
quiz.explain: Shortcrust is the crisp pastry used for tarts and pies.

days.title: Baking Problems and Fixes
days.goal: Fix the commonest baking problems.

video.title: 10 Minutes Snack! Easy Flaky Meat Pie with Puff Pastry

steps: Bread did not rise? Your yeast may be old, or the water was too hot.
Cake sank in the middle? The oven door was opened too early.
Pastry is soggy? The filling was too wet or the oven was too cool.
Bread is hard? It was over-baked or had too little water.
Write down each problem and fix, so you learn from it.
days.task: Pick one baking problem you have had and fix it today.
days.challenge: Bake a loaf and write down everything that went right and wrong.

quiz.q: Why does hot water kill yeast?
options: It makes it rise too fast
quiz.explain: Yeast is alive. Very hot water kills it, so the dough will not rise.

quiz.q: Why did the cake sink?
options: The oven door was opened too early
quiz.explain: Opening the door early lets hot air out and the cake falls.

quiz.q: What makes pastry soggy?
options: A wet filling or an oven that is too cool
quiz.explain: Wet filling and low heat stop the pastry from crisping.

days.title: Week 3 Project: A Bakery Table
days.goal: Bake a table of bread, buns, and a pie for your household.

video.title: I Stopped Rolling Dough — Now I Bake Dinner Pies This Way

steps: Pick the menu: a loaf, buns, and a dinner pie.
Write a shopping list with costs.
Start the bread first since it needs rising time.
Bake the pie while the bread cools.
Serve everything together and get feedback.
days.task: Bake a loaf, buns, and a pie in one session.
days.challenge: Cost the whole table and work out the price per person.

quiz.q: Why start the bread first?
quiz.explain: Bread needs an hour or more to rise, so it starts first.

quiz.q: What makes a good bakery table?
options: A mix of bread, buns, and something savoury
quiz.explain: A mix gives everyone something to enjoy.

quiz.q: Why cost the table?
options: So you know what to charge if you sell it
quiz.explain: Costing turns baking into a business.

project.title: Bake a Bakery Table
project.brief: Bake a loaf, a tray of buns, and a dinner pie, served together.
checks: Three different bakes made
Bread risen well and baked through
Buns soft and golden
Pie golden with a crisp base
Everything served together
Costs worked out and feedback collected

days.title: Packaging Baked Goods
days.goal: Pack your bakes so they stay fresh and look good.

video.title: Spanish Puff Pastry Meat Pie (Murcia-Style)

steps: Let bakes cool fully before packing. Warm bakes go soggy in a bag.
Use clean paper bags or food boxes.
Label with the name, the date, and the ingredients.
Keep bread in a cloth bag or paper bag, not plastic, so the crust stays crisp.
Store cakes in a sealed box to keep them moist.
days.task: Pack a batch of bakes as if for a customer.
days.challenge: Give a packed box to someone and ask for feedback on the look.

quiz.q: Why cool bakes before packing?
options: Warm bakes make steam and go soggy
quiz.explain: Warm food in a closed bag makes steam, and steam makes crusts soft.

quiz.q: Why not store bread in plastic?
options: Plastic traps moisture and softens the crust
quiz.explain: Plastic traps moisture, so a crisp crust goes soft.

quiz.q: What should a label say?
quiz.explain: Labels tell the buyer what it is, when it was made, and what is in it.

days.title: Baking on a Budget
days.goal: Bake well without spending too much.

video.title: Nigerian Puff Puff Recipe: How to Make Puff Puff

steps: Buy flour, yeast, and sugar in bigger bags. They cost less per kilo.
Use what you have: bananas going soft become banana bread.
Bake in batches so the oven is never half empty.
Use cheaper fillings like vegetables and beans for pies.
Cost each bake and keep a simple record.
days.task: Plan a week of bakes using what you already have plus one shop.
days.challenge: Cost your week of bakes and cut it by 10 percent.

quiz.q: Why buy flour in bigger bags?
quiz.explain: Bigger bags cost less for each kilo.

quiz.q: Why bake in batches?
options: A full oven uses gas better than a half-empty one
quiz.explain: Baking more at once saves gas and time.

quiz.q: What is a good cheap pie filling?
quiz.explain: Vegetables and beans are cheap, filling, and tasty.

days.title: Gluten-Free and Healthier Bakes
days.goal: Bake lighter options for people who need them.

video.title: You'll Never Need Another Puff Puff Recipe Again | Street Snacks Ep. 17

steps: Try a flour mix made for gluten-free baking.
Use less sugar and add fruit for sweetness.
Use oil instead of butter for a lighter bake.
Add oats or seeds for extra fibre and crunch.
Label your bakes clearly so buyers know what is in them.
days.task: Bake a gluten-free or lighter loaf.
days.challenge: Bake a low-sugar banana bread and compare the taste.

quiz.q: What does gluten-free mean?
options: No gluten, the protein in wheat
quiz.explain: Gluten is the protein in wheat. Gluten-free bakes use other flours.

quiz.q: What adds sweetness without much sugar?
quiz.explain: Ripe fruit like banana adds natural sweetness.

quiz.q: Why label your bakes?
options: So people with allergies know what is safe
quiz.explain: Clear labels keep people with allergies safe.

days.title: Festive Bakes: Christmas and Parties
days.goal: Plan and bake for a party or festival.

video.title: Puff Puff (West African Doughnuts)

steps: Plan the menu a week ahead: bread, snacks, and a cake.
Bake breads and pies in advance and freeze them.
Fry puff puff and doughnuts on the day so they are fresh.
Make a big snack box for guests.
Serve with drinks and take photos.
days.task: Plan a party baking menu and bake one item from it.
days.challenge: Bake and freeze a loaf in advance, then thaw and check the taste.

quiz.q: What bakes freeze well?
quiz.explain: Bread and pies freeze well. Fried snacks do not.

quiz.q: What should be made fresh on the day?
quiz.explain: Fried snacks go soft if made early, so fry them on the day.

quiz.q: Why plan a week ahead?
options: So you have time to shop and bake without stress
quiz.explain: Planning ahead stops last-minute stress.

days.title: Your Signature Bake
days.goal: Choose and perfect one bake you can make brilliantly.

video.title: Quarantine Cooking: African Doughnuts

steps: Pick the bake your household loves most from this course.
Write the recipe in your own words with exact amounts.
Bake it again, timing every step and noting problems.
Fix the problems and bake it once more.
Get someone new to taste it and give honest feedback.
days.task: Bake your signature bake and write the final recipe down.
days.challenge: Bake it for someone new and record what they say.

quiz.q: What is a signature bake?
options: A bake you can make brilliantly every time
A bake with a fancy name
quiz.explain: A signature bake is one you have mastered.

quiz.q: Why write the recipe in your own words?
options: So you truly understand it and can repeat it
quiz.explain: Writing it yourself proves you understand each step.

quiz.q: Why get a new person to taste it?
quiz.explain: People who know you may be polite. New tasters are honest.

days.title: Selling Your Bakes: First Steps
days.goal: Take your first steps toward selling your bakes.

video.title: EXTRA CRISPY Bread in 5 Minutes! No Kneading, Just Mix and Bake

steps: Pick 2 or 3 bakes to sell. Do not sell everything at once.
Set your prices from your costing work.
Take clear photos of your bakes in good light.
Tell friends and family first. Ask them to share.
Take orders in advance so you bake only what is sold.
days.task: Take photos of your best bakes and show them to three people.
days.challenge: Take one real order, even a small one, and deliver it on time.

quiz.q: Why start with only 2 or 3 bakes?
options: A small menu is easier to make well and cost
quiz.explain: A small menu keeps quality high and costing simple.

quiz.q: Why take orders in advance?
options: So you bake only what is sold and waste nothing
quiz.explain: Advance orders mean no waste and no guessing.

quiz.q: Why do photos matter?
options: Clear photos help people decide to buy
quiz.explain: People buy with their eyes first. Good photos sell bakes.

days.title: Keeping Records: Orders and Money
days.goal: Keep simple records of your baking business.

video.title: Easiest Homemade White Bread Recipe: No Fancy Tools Needed

steps: Write down every order: what, how many, who, and when.
Write down what you spent and what you earned.
Work out your profit each week.
Note which bakes sell best and which do not.
Keep your money for baking separate from your spending money.
days.task: Start a simple order book today, on paper or on your phone.
days.challenge: Work out your profit from one batch of bakes.

quiz.q: Why write down every order?
options: So nothing is forgotten and you know what to bake
quiz.explain: Written orders stop mistakes and show what sells.

quiz.q: What is profit?
options: What is left after costs are taken from what you earned
quiz.explain: Profit is what remains after you pay for ingredients, gas, and packaging.

quiz.q: Why keep baking money separate?
options: So you always know if baking is making money
quiz.explain: Separate money shows the true profit of your baking.

days.title: Revision: The Baker's Skills Check
days.goal: Revisit the core skills of the course.

video.title: HOW This 1-Minute Dough Makes Better Bread Than Your Bakery

steps: Bake a white loaf from memory, without the recipe.
Make a pastry by rubbing butter into flour.
Name three things yeast needs to work.
Check your costing: cost one bake from memory.
List your three strongest bakes and one to improve.
days.task: Bake a full set from memory: a loaf and a snack.
days.challenge: Teach one bake from this course to a friend or family member.

quiz.q: What three things does yeast need?
quiz.explain: Yeast needs warmth, something to eat, and time to make gas.

quiz.q: Why bake from memory?
options: It proves you really know the steps
quiz.explain: Baking without a recipe shows the skills are truly learned.

quiz.q: Why teach a bake to someone else?
options: Teaching proves you really know it
quiz.explain: If you can teach it, you truly understand it.

days.title: Capstone Prep: Plan Your Final Bake
days.goal: Plan your capstone baking table and gather everything you need.

video.title: The Easiest Sourdough Bread for Beginners! No Kneading, Just 4 Ingredients

steps: Choose your capstone menu: a bread, a pastry, and a sweet bake.
Write the full shopping list with costs.
Write the baking order, starting with the dough that needs the longest rise.
Check you have every tool and ingredient.
Do a trial run of the hardest bake if you have time.
days.task: Write your complete capstone plan and cost it.
days.challenge: Do a trial run of your hardest capstone bake today.

quiz.q: What should your capstone show?
options: Everything you learned: bread, pastry, costing, and timing
quiz.explain: The capstone proves the whole course.

quiz.q: Why start with the longest-rising dough?
options: So everything finishes at the same time
quiz.explain: Long-rising dough starts first so all bakes finish together.

quiz.q: Why do a trial run?
options: To find problems before the real bake
quiz.explain: A trial run finds problems while there is still time to fix them.

capstone.title: The Baker's Table: Bread, Pastry and Something Sweet
capstone.brief: Bake a full table for your household or customers: a loaf of bread, a pastry (meat pie or dinner pie), and a sweet bake (banana bread or doughnuts). Cost the whole table, pack it neatly, and serve or deliver it on time.
checks: Menu planned with a shopping list and costs
Bread risen well, baked through, with a good crust
Pastry golden and flaky, not soggy
Sweet bake cooked through and tasty
Everything packed neatly and labelled
Costs worked out and price per item set
Feedback collected from at least one person who tasted the bakes
deliverables: A photo of the finished baking table
Your written menu with the shopping list and costs
Your baking order, starting with the longest-rising dough
Your signature bake recipe written in your own words
A short note on what you learned and what you will improve next
